<doc file="docs/contributing.md" section="Development proxy setup" lines="182-235">
 182| ## Development proxy setup
 183| 
 184| To test and debug requests via a proxy it's best to run a proxy server locally.
 185| Any server should do but HTTPCore's test suite uses
 186| [`mitmproxy`](https://mitmproxy.org/) which is written in Python, it's fully
 187| featured and has excellent UI and tools for introspection of requests.
 188| 
 189| You can install `mitmproxy` using `pip install mitmproxy` or [several
 190| other ways](https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/overview-installation/).
 191| 
 192| `mitmproxy` does require setting up local TLS certificates for HTTPS requests,
 193| as its main purpose is to allow developers to inspect requests that pass through
 194| it. We can set them up follows:
 195| 
 196| 1. [`pip install trustme-cli`](https://github.com/sethmlarson/trustme-cli/).
 197| 2. `trustme-cli -i example.org www.example.org`, assuming you want to test
 198| connecting to that domain, this will create three files: `server.pem`,
 199| `server.key` and `client.pem`.
 200| 3. `mitmproxy` requires a PEM file that includes the private key and the
 201| certificate so we need to concatenate them:
 202| `cat server.key server.pem > server.withkey.pem`.
 203| 4. Start the proxy server `mitmproxy --certs server.withkey.pem`, or use the
 204| [other mitmproxy commands](https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/) with different
 205| UI options.
 206| 
 207| At this point the server is ready to start serving requests, you'll need to
 208| configure HTTPX as described in the
 209| [proxy section](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/proxies/#http-proxies) and
 210| the [SSL certificates section](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/ssl/),
 211| this is where our previously generated `client.pem` comes in:
 212| 
 213| ```
 214| import httpx
 215| 
 216| with httpx.Client(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:8080/", verify="/path/to/client.pem") as client:
 217|     response = client.get("https://example.org")
 218|     print(response.status_code)  # should print 200
 219| ```
 220| 
 221| Note, however, that HTTPS requests will only succeed to the host specified
 222| in the SSL/TLS certificate we generated, HTTPS requests to other hosts will
 223| raise an error like:
 224| 
 225| ```
 226| ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate
 227| verify failed: Hostname mismatch, certificate is not valid for
 228| 'duckduckgo.com'. (_ssl.c:1108)
 229| ```
 230| 
 231| If you want to make requests to more hosts you'll need to regenerate the
 232| certificates and include all the hosts you intend to connect to in the
 233| seconds step, i.e.
 234| 
 235| `trustme-cli -i example.org www.example.org duckduckgo.com www.duckduckgo.com`
</doc>
